deep_dive.title: SecFD-FL: Frequency-Decoupled Federated Learning with Secure Aggregation for Charging Load Forecasting in Internet of Electric Vehicles
deep_dive.abstract: Accurate charging load forecasting is essential for the reliability and efficiency of the Internet of Electric Vehicles (IoEV), yet it is challenging on two fronts: charging demand is highly stochastic, and the data collected by distributed sensors is privacy-sensitive. Although federated learning (FL) preserves data privacy, collaborative training still remains vulnerable to an honest-but-curious server that can invert shared model updates to reconstruct private data. To address both data volatility and privacy concerns, we propose SecFD-FL, a frequency-decoupled federated learning framework for IoEV comprising: 1) a dual-stream gated recurrent unit (GRU) network that separately models short-term and long-term charging load volatility, and 2) a lightweight secure aggregation layer for privacy preservation. Specifically, the secure aggregation layer employs a zero-sum additive masking protocol that perturbs each client's upload with high-variance noise, preventing the server from reconstructing private data while preserving the exact aggregate. Extensive experiments have been conducted on both EV-level and charging station-level using real datasets. The experiment results show that SecFD-FL reduces global RMSE by up to 60% over centralized baselines, achieving Jain's fairness up to 0.991 across clients, and reduces DLG-attack reconstruction correlation by 8 times to 15 times relative to FedAvg -- all with no additional per-round communication cost beyond a one-time key exchange.

deep_dive.title: Probabilistic Forecasting of Electric Vehicle Charging in a Time-varying Hierarchical Infrastructure
deep_dive.abstract: Uncertainty quantification for electric vehicle (EV) charging demand is essential to turn the increasing pressure of EV adoption on power systems into a source of flexibility. We study a large-scale dataset of public charging stations in Scotland, where demand exhibits a hierarchical structure, organized across multiple aggregation levels, from individual charging points to regional and national scales. The charging infrastructure is continuously evolving, with new stations deployed and existing ones occasionally removed, which calls for forecasting and uncertainty quantification methods tailored to this evolving structure. To address these challenges, we combine hierarchical forecasting with recent advances in conformal prediction with missing data. The conformal procedures considered produce valid prediction intervals at every node of the hierarchy and the algorithm CP-MNR-Nested successfully accounts for the time-varying hierarchical structure of the data.

deep_dive.title: Co-Optimization of Scheduling, Control, and Incentivization of Electric Vehicles for Improving Power System Stability
deep_dive.abstract: We present a finite-horizon, greedy heuristic-based co-optimization and optimal control framework that jointly determines the optimized charging rates, charging times, and an optimal charging control law for electric vehicles (EVs) to improve both voltage stability and small-signal dynamic performance of a power distribution system. The proposed strategy encourages EV drivers to be flexible in choosing their charging rates and times through monetary incentivization under a fixed budget. The design is validated using the IEEE 33-bus distribution system model with ten EV charging stations (EVCSs). Results show that incentivizing drivers to settle for lower charging rates, implemented by a wait-and-save strategy, and rescheduling their charging times strategically can significantly improve the voltage stability index (VSI) of the system as well as the damping factors for the mid-frequency oscillation modes seen in the DC-link bus voltage.

deep_dive.title: Degradation Aware V2G Dispatch for Co-Optimization of Parking Facility and Edge Data Center Located in the Airport Campus
deep_dive.abstract: This paper studies an airport campus where long stay EV parking, airport buildings, and an AI data center share a single grid connection. The campus pays a commercial electricity tariff that charges for both the energy used and the highest power drawn during peak hours. Parked EVs can send power back to the campus through vehicle to grid (V2G) chargers and lower this peak. This paper proposes a two stage method. In the first stage, a linear program schedules EV charging and discharging to maximize the operator's profit and also sets a fixed daily payment to EV owners. In the second stage, a search chooses the share of energy savings paid to owners. The model guarantees that every owner is paid enough to take part, pays for battery wear so that EVs discharge only when it is worth the wear, and assigns charging ports on a first come, first served basis. In the case study, 400 V2G chargers are added to 1200 existing Level 2 chargers, serving 5000 expected sessions under summer and winter rates. In a summer week, V2G raises operator profit by $4978 compared with smart charging and lowers the high peak demand by 4400 kW (9%). The best contract gives owners 70% of the energy savings and earns 21% more than a fixed payment alone. Doubling the V2G ports to 800 lowers the peak further but reduces profit, because owner payments grow faster than the savings. V2G pays back within 10 years if a bidirectional charger costs less than about $1800 more than a standard one. Compared with a 5 MW/10 MWh stationary battery, V2G cuts more peak demand at $409 of investment per kW instead of $1522 and needs no extra land, while the battery does not pay back within its lifetime.

deep_dive.title: OpenHail: An Event-Driven Gymnasium Environment for Electric Ride-Hailing Fleet Control
deep_dive.abstract: Machine-learning policies have attracted increasing interest for ride-hailing fleet control in recent years. Reinforcement learning, in particular, requires a structured simulation environment that specifies observations, actions, rewards, and decision epochs for training and evaluation. For electric fleets, this environment must also capture the interaction among stochastic demand, vehicle operations, and capacitated charging infrastructure. We present OpenHail, an open-source Gymnasium environment for joint control of electric ride-hailing fleets. Its fixed-size observation--action interface exposes request assignment, repositioning, and charging to a single policy. The event-driven simulator represents requests with pickup deadlines, vehicle job queues, battery dynamics, and finite-capacity charging facilities with first-in--first-out queues. A configurable decision-epoch mechanism separates internal simulator events from policy interactions, supporting event-driven, periodic, hybrid, and policy-requested control within the same operational model. The software provides seeded instances, feasible-action utilities, evaluation tools, operational metrics, and baseline policies. The source code is available at https://github.com/tommaso-schettini/openhail.

deep_dive.title: Price-Optimized EV and Heat-Pump Scheduling Can Exceed Uncoordinated Feeder Peaks
deep_dive.abstract: Electric vehicles and heat pumps add large, time-flexible loads to low-voltage distribution feeders. When each household independently minimizes its own charging cost against the same electricity price, this flexible demand piles into the cheapest hours, and the resulting synchronization can stress the feeder more than uncoordinated operation does. This work quantifies that effect on a rural low-voltage feeder (97 buses, 250 kVA transformer) across 160 simulation runs spanning seven scenarios, four seasons, and electric-vehicle, heat-pump, and photovoltaic penetration from 0 to 90 %. At 30 % penetration of each device, this decentralized cost minimization drives the transformer to 253 % of rated capacity, more than twice the level of uncoordinated charging, and up to 478 % at 90 % electric-vehicle penetration, with the first undervoltage violations at the far end of the longest feeder arm. The ranking is device-mix dependent: each 30 pp of heat-pump penetration adds about twelve times more to the price-based peak than to any fixed schedule, so price-based scheduling becomes the worst strategy once heat pumps are present. Only a central schedule that explicitly caps the transformer removes these demand-driven violations, while at high photovoltaic penetration a summer floor from midday reverse power flow bounds what any demand-side strategy can achieve. A regulated time-variable grid tariff added to the spot price provides no relief for heat-pump-driven synchronization and only marginal relief for electric-vehicle-driven synchronization in autumn. The simulation and optimization code is available at https://github.com/lukas-wagner/SynchronizationEffectsAnalysis.

quick_skim.title: Models of Electric Vehicle Charging Demands in Distribution Grid Operation: A Review
quick_skim.abstract: The rapid integration of electric vehicles (EVs) into the transportation system has introduced a new class of load into power distribution systems (PDS), i.e., EV charging demand (EVCD). The spatiotemporal variability of EVCD poses fundamental challenges for distribution system operators (DSOs), particularly in ensuring secure and reliable network operation. Accurately representing EVCD as a parameter within the distribution optimal power flow (DOPF) problem is a prerequisite for reliable, cost-efficient PDS operation, yet no universally accepted modeling framework has emerged. The existing contributions span a wide spectrum of assumptions, mathematical formulations, and solution paradigms. This article presents a systematic review of methods and models employed to represent EVCD within DOPF frameworks from the DSO's operational perspective. The existing EVCD modeling methods are classified into two primary categories based on EVCD representation: deterministic models and uncertainty-aware models. The two main categories are further divided into several subcategories. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive review on models for integrating EVCD into PDS operation and planning.

quick_skim.title: L2R-EV: Learning What to Repair in Electric Ride-Pooling with Finite Charger Queues
quick_skim.abstract: Electric ride-pooling must jointly manage passenger service, routes, batteries, and finite chargers; a locally useful relocation can reduce later service. We introduce a discrete-event ride-pooling simulator with ordered passenger stops, pickup and ride-time constraints, battery reserves, charger travel, and finite first-come, first-served (FCFS) charging queues. On top of a common dispatcher, we add a learned repair layer that moves uncollected passengers between vehicles, uses a supervised score to estimate later effects, and uses a two-stage proximal-policy-optimization (PPO) policy to focus computation on promising moves. Every executed move must satisfy route, battery, and time constraints and provide an immediate route-cost improvement. For larger instances, we limit the number of candidate moves and apply several non-conflicting repairs at once. On 12 held-out Manhattan episodes with 100 requests, 30 EVs, and one plug per station, supervised repair reduces operational cost by 6.57\% versus no repair (12/12 wins) and serves 74.92 rather than 72.75 requests. Two-stage PPO stays within 1.43\% of supervised repair with 95.4\% fewer exact trials, while our experiments scale to 8,000 requests and 2,400 EVs with cost reductions across all three larger development settings. Queue-aware charging reduces waiting by 41.0\%; under a declared 1.5-kW queue-idle load, operational electricity per served request falls 1.73\%.

quick_skim.title: The missing price feedback: Why studies overstate local peaks from synchronized home batteries under dynamic pricing
quick_skim.abstract: Existing studies consistently find that home batteries and electric vehicles optimized against real-time electricity prices create new load peaks in local distribution grids, because all assets respond to the same price signal in sync. However, all but one of the 18 studies reviewed here treat wholesale prices as exogenous. This paper argues that treating prices as non-responsive biases the result: in reality, charging in low-price hours raises the wholesale price, which dampens the incentive to charge. I test this by simulating households with rooftop solar and home batteries under a spot-based retail tariff, calibrated to German data for 2025 with a model of equilibrium wholesale prices. With exogenous prices, my results confirm the finding from the previous literature: synchronous charging pushes the coincident import peak of the local grid to 83% above its no-battery level. With endogenous prices, the same fleet leaves the peak 6% below the no-battery benchmark. In other words, treating prices as endogenous reduces the coincident peak at high battery penetration nearly by half. This finding is robust across alternative price functions and exogenous price paths, different measures of the coincident peak, 25 scenario variations and three historical years. I conclude that new local peaks remain possible, particularly in grids where battery deployment runs ahead of the national average, but the risk and magnitude are considerably smaller than the existing literature suggests.

quick_skim.title: Distributionally Robust Chance-Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Home Energy Management under Electric Vehicle Uncertainty
quick_skim.abstract: The electrification of residential energy systems and adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) create demand-side flexibility. However, random driving behaviour makes it difficult to ensure EV readiness at departure and maintain thermal comfort. To address this, we formulate residential scheduling as a distributionally robust (DR) chance-constrained Markov decision process, whose 2-Wasserstein ambiguity set guards against tail risk and distribution shift in EV behaviour. The intractable DR chance constraint is then replaced by a sufficient tightened expectation constraint under the nominal distribution. The resulting problem is solved by a Lagrangian soft actor--critic with distributional cost critics, and an online boundary guard enforces EV reachability and thermal comfort within the actuator limits at every step. Five controllers are compared over one year in Wellington, New Zealand, under a degraded forecast. The proposed controller is the cheapest controller that meets the EV target on every day and both chance constraints under forecast error and random driving behaviour. Compared with the rule-based baseline, the only other controller to do so, it lowers the annual cost by 8.6% and the comfort violation hours by 69%. The ablation study confirms that the boundary guard ensures pointwise feasibility within the actuator limits, and the DR chance constraint reduces tail risk.

quick_skim.title: Adaptive Operator Selection in Bilevel Large Neighborhood Search for Electric Autonomous Dial-a-Ride Problem under Uncertainty
quick_skim.abstract: The electric autonomous dial-a-ride problem (EADARP) extends the classical dial-a-ride problem by incorporating battery and charging constraints for electric vehicles. In practice, travel-time uncertainty can cause violations of time-window constraints. Large neighborhood search is effective for solving the EADARP, but its performance can depend on the choice of insertion operator during the repair phase. This paper investigates insertion-operator selection within a bilevel large neighborhood search framework for deterministic and chance-constrained variants of the EADARP. In the chance-constrained variant, arc travel times are modeled as independent normally distributed random variables, and upper time-window constraints are enforced probabilistically. We consider six selection methods, namely fixed greedy insertion, fixed regret-based insertion, random selection, a deterministic state-based rule, performance-adaptive ALNS selection, and LLM-based state-aware selection. Experimental results show comparable performance on smaller instances, while differences become more evident on larger and more constrained instances. There is no single strategy that performs best across all instances, and the relative performance of the LLM-based, rule-based, and ALNS strategies varies with the problem instance and experimental setting.

quick_skim.title: Optimal Control of a Non-Stationary Inventory-Queue, with Applications to EV-Battery Swapping
quick_skim.abstract: We study a non-stationary queueing system with multiple parallel servers and a finite buffer capacity, over a finite planning horizon. Motivated by an operation that is central to an EV (electric vehicle) battery-swapping station -- how to best manage the charging of batteries swapped off from EVs, we develop a continuous-time MDP (Markov decision process) approach to the problem. The main technical challenge is to allow both the arrival rate and the service-cost rate to be functions of time with jumps at discrete time points, key features of the EV swapping station's operation. We derive an exact and explicit threshold structure that characterizes the optimal control policy. Moreover, we give conditions under which the thresholds are monotone over time, and with respect to key system parameters such as service and buffer capacities. Extensive numerical experiments are carried out to supplement as well as validate the theoretical results, and also to illustrate the robustness of the threshold structure in practical implementations.

quick_skim.title: Optimizing Airport Electric Ground Support Fleets with Digital-Twin-Guided Predictive Control
quick_skim.abstract: Electrifying airport ground operations is a key step toward reducing aviation-related emissions, but it makes task assignment and charging coordination strongly coupled in real time. This paper develops a digital twin of airport ground handling operations for electric ground-support vehicles (EGSVs), combining an agent-based model of airport operations with live flight-schedule updates and vehicle-energy dynamics. On this platform, we compare three control strategies for EGSV dispatching and charging: a rule-based heuristic, a rolling-horizon model predictive controller (MPC), and a Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) controller. The controllers are evaluated on three representative Schiphol Airport operating days and for multiple fleet sizes. The results show a clear trade-off between delays and energy use. Across all tested scenarios, MCTS yields the lowest average flight delay, with a pooled delay of 4.09 min, improving on the heuristic and MPC controllers by 64.7\% and 31.5\%, but at an increased energy consumption of 1\% and 0.3\%, respectively.The MPC and MCTS controllers coordinate charging more effectively throughout the day and reduce the peak charging infrastructure required by 6.0 and 4.7 charger units, respectively. Additionally, we find more vehicles can result in lower overall energy consumption and lower charging infrastructure requirements for all controllers. These findings highlight the value of digital twins not only as offline design evaluation tools, but also as practical environments for real-time control policies in electrified airport operations.

quick_skim.title: Hours-of-service-aware siting of charging and battery-swapping stations for long-haul electric trucks under adoption uncertainty
quick_skim.abstract: Planning en-route charging and battery-swapping infrastructure for long-haul battery-electric trucks (BETs) requires models that reflect how trucks actually operate. This paper develops a mixed-integer programming framework that jointly sites charging or swapping stations and schedules each truck's charging, swapping and mandatory driver rest, so that charging time overlaps with regulated rest instead of being added to it. Energy use is derived segment by segment from road terrain with a tractive-force model, and the truck battery is modelled as a set of independently swappable packs. Staged investment under uncertain BET adoption is formulated as a multistage stochastic program with Markovian demand and solved by stochastic dual dynamic integer programming (SDDiP) with Lagrangian cuts; we show that the Lagrangian multipliers can be bounded by each station's annualised cost without weakening the cuts. Applied to twelve freight corridors on Australia's East Coast, the algorithm jointly optimises charging and battery-swapping events as well as mandatory break events. A +/- 30\% change in adoption alters the final charge-only network by only -12\% to +13\% of stations, with over 95\% of stations built by the second stage. Hedging against uncertainty mainly changes which sites are chosen (71\% overlap with a deterministic rolling-horizon model), not when they are built.

quick_skim.title: Predictive Rerouting of Connected and Automated Vehicles Using Traffic and Charging Demand Forecasts
quick_skim.abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of predictive rerouting of connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) in mixed traffic with electric vehicle charging demand. We provide a framework that combines a diffusion convolutional recurrent neural network (DCRNN) with a routing policy that accounts for congestion, CO2 emissions, route length, and charging demand. The DCRNN uses historical network observations to forecast traffic conditions and charging demand. These forecasts are then used to evaluate feasible alternative routes for eligible CAVs. A route change is accepted when the alternative preserves connectivity to the original destination and improves the prescribed route cost. We evaluate the proposed framework in SUMO under controlled traffic disruptions at five CAV penetration levels, ranging from 5% to 45%. We compare its performance with K-shortest-path routing, predictive-density routing, V2X proactive routing, and a reference scenario without rerouting. In the considered scenarios, the proposed framework reduces the average travel-time index by approximately 1.8% relative to the reference scenario and achieves the lowest average travel-time index, highest average speed, and lowest aggregate CO2 emissions among the active routing methods. Across all five penetration levels, it accepts 41 route changes, compared with 146 for K-shortest-path routing and 153 for V2X proactive routing. The reference scenario retains lower aggregate emissions and distance traveled, illustrating the tradeoff between congestion reduction and the additional travel associated with rerouting.

quick_skim.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Pricing and Operation for Hybrid Electric and Hydrogen Vehicle Stations
quick_skim.abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) and hydrogen fuel cell vehi- cles (HFCVs) are promising technologies in the efforts to reduce carbon emissions. Challenges such as limited infrastructure, con- sumer dissatisfaction, and electrical grid strain inhibit progress in the adoption of these technologies. A zero emission vehicle (ZEV) station, capable of handling EVs and HFCVs, addresses these challenges by focusing on maximizing station profit and consumer utility, while minimizing grid impacts. The purpose of this research is to develop a realistic simulation of a ZEV station that is capable of handling real-time pricing decisions enabled by reinforcement learning (RL) and to compare the performance of the RL agent to static pricing methods. After training, the RL agent gains 10.83% greater station profit than the baseline manual parameter search. This work serves as a useful tool for ZEV station owners when handling complex pricing and purchasing decisions.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 面向电动与氢燃料车辆的零排放补给站需在基础设施有限与电网压力下兼顾站点利润和用户效用。作者构建可处理实时定价决策的混合能源站仿真环境，并用强化学习智能体动态调整价格与运营策略。与静态定价方法的对比显示学习型策略能更好地平衡收益、用户满意度与电网影响。该研究为多能源补给站的实时定价与运营调度提供了可复用的仿真与决策框架。
